title: Release strategies: blue-green, canary and feature flags

videos.script: Every deploy so far stopped the old program and started the new one. For a moment, nothing answered. {{gap}} This lesson measures that moment, and then removes it in three different ways. Each one buys something different. {{three}} First, two productions and a switch. The new release waits beside the old one, and a router moves every customer across at once. You will watch it move two thousand requests without dropping one, and then watch one request in twenty fail on the new side. {{switch}} Going back takes three milliseconds, because the old side never stopped. {{back}} Then the same release as a canary, at one request in ten. The same bug reaches two customers instead of seventy-seven. And you will see why eight requests prove nothing, with a little arithmetic. {{canary}} Last, feature flags. The code goes to production switched off, and customers meet it later, ten percent at a time, and always the same ten percent. {{flags}} The lesson ends with a table: what each strategy costs, and how to choose. {{choose}}
